chapter: Philadelphia, Atlantic City and the war years
title: Billy Douglas, the Connecticut trumpeter who left Earl Hines
summary: Billy Douglas, an arranger from New Haven, was lost to drink when Earl Hines was leaving New York.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Billy Douglas?
Billy Douglas -- but he could arrange too.
Well, where -- you say from Connecticut?
That's right. Born and raised in Connecticut.
Well, there was another Billy Douglas;
Well, this Billy Douglass--
There was Billy Douglas the trumpet player --
Yeah, this is a trumpet player.
(Simultaneous remarks)
Yes, left Earl Hines' band with (unintelligible). I think they played Boston and came back to Connecticut and stopped in -- that's his home. And he's --
What town in Connecticut did he live in?
I think he's from New Haven.
Well --
Because Kenneth Roane is from -- Kenneth Roane is not from New Haven. Kenneth Roane is from the biggest city up there in Connecticut.
Well, there's Bridgeport.
Not, Bridgeport. That's way down on --
Hartford --
Hartford --
Yeah, that's --
-- I think that's Kenneth Roane's home, Hartford.
Well, I mean the thing about him,
did he die?
Kenneth?
Billy Douglas?

Yes, he did. They -- here's what happened. When -- they came back when Earl Hines was on the way back to New York, and Billy could naturally -- Billy stopped off in his home town, New Haven, and I guess he got taken away, because that juice got the best of him when Earl Hines was looking for him when Earl Hines was going to leave out of New York, going to Chicago -- no Billy.
